title: Ibn al-Haytham (Alhazen, 965–c. 1040) — The Nile Dam Gamble, Feigned Madness Under Caliph al-Hakim, and the House-Arrest Camera Obscura

teenKit.tldr: Ibn al-Haytham faked his own madness for a decade under a furious ruler just to survive, while secretly inventing the scientific method and figuring out how light enters the human eye.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Every time you snap a digital photo, use a smartphone screen, or trust medical research backed by experiments instead of guesswork, you are using the rules of evidence that al-Haytham locked down in his dark room.
keyTakeaways: Al-Haytham boldly promised to control the flooding Nile River with a massive dam, but when he saw the actual site at Aswan, he realized it was physically impossible and had to fake insanity to escape the wrath of a lethal caliph.
Instead of blindly trusting ancient authorities like Aristotle or Euclid, he insisted that ideas must be physically tested through rigorous, repeatable experiments.

His seven-volume masterpiece, the Kitab al-Manazir (Book of Optics), completely flipped human understanding by proving that light bounces off objects and enters our eyes, rather than shooting out of our eyeballs like laser beams.

vocab.meaning: A darkened room or box with a tiny pinhole on one side that projects an upside-down, real-world image onto the opposite wall using light.
A high-tech laboratory method used to figure out the 3D atomic structure of complex molecules by bouncing X-rays off crystallized proteins.
A light-sensitive protein found in the retina of your eyes that kickstarts vision the exact second a photon of light hits it.
The golden rule of science that states knowledge comes strictly from sensory experience, observation, and hands-on testing rather than pure thought or ancient tradition.

quiz.question: Why did Ibn al-Haytham end up under decade-long house arrest in Cairo?
options: He stole royal gold from the caliph's private treasury.
He failed to build the impossible Nile dam he promised and faked insanity to save his life from the volatile Caliph al-Hakim.
He refused to translate ancient Greek texts into Arabic.
He started a violent political rebellion in the streets of Basra.
quiz.explanation: He realized the Aswan dam project was a physical impossibility too late, so he feigned madness to escape execution by the erratic Fatimid ruler.

quiz.question: What was the massive breakthrough al-Haytham made regarding how human vision works?
options: He proved the eyes shoot out invisible beams of light to touch objects.
He discovered that vision is entirely controlled by brain waves rather than light.
He proved that light reflects off external objects and enters the eye to form an image.
He showed that human eyes only function correctly in complete darkness.
quiz.explanation: He shattered centuries of Greek dogma by proving light travels from objects into our eyes, not the other way around.

quiz.question: What structural protein data bank reference (PDB) is used to track the exact moment light triggers human vision at an atomic level?
quiz.explanation: PDB 1U19 provides the precise crystal structure of rhodopsin to show how a single photon trips the retinal switch inside your eye.
